ruled_out_vectors.vector: Reentrancy via _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers — _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) clears flags during fee transfers
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: _setReentrancyFlags preserves ENTERED bit (bit 1). All nonReentrant* modifiers check ENTERED, so reentrancy is blocked even after flags are cleared. See TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags._nonReentrantBefore().

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Cross-operation reentrancy via different guard flag types (SWAP vs LIQUIDITY vs FLASHLOAN)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: ENTERED bit is THE global reentrancy lock. Different flags (bits 2-11) are informational only. _nonReentrantBefore always sets ENTERED and checks it regardless of which flags are requested.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: HOOK-001 transient storage stale read (DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT) for profit extraction
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Already classified as CP-001 (Low). Stale value only affects pricing bounds accept/reject gate in afterSwap for direct swaps. Actual swap amounts are computed by AMM math, not the hook. Impact limited to governance/config enforcement, not direct value extraction.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Flash loan + view function desync — getPoolState returns stale reserves during flash loan
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool reserves are NOT updated during flash loan (borrowed tokens are returned). Any integrator reading getPoolState sees correct reserves. Balance-of discrepancy is inherent to flash loans, not a protocol bug.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: collectHookFeesByHook without nonReentrant modifier exploitable during swaps
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Correctly uses flag-based routing: queues during swaps (SWAP_GUARD_FLAG set), reverts during flash loans (FLASHLOAN_GUARD_FLAG set), transfers immediately otherwise. During flag-cleared state in _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers, CEI pattern in _transferHookFeesByHook prevents double-spending (tokensOwed decremented before external call).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: _storeNonTokenHookFees hash key mismatch — uses hash(tokenFor, tokenFor) vs _transferHookFeesByHook hash(tokenFor, tokenFee)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Intentional design. For pool/liquidity hooks, the fee token IS the associated token (tokenFor == tokenFee). collectHookFeesByHook uses msg.sender as hook address, preventing cross-hook fee theft.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Fee denomination mismatch (CP-EXT-001 pattern) — output fees stored with wrong denomination
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Traced through _applySwapByInputOutputFees. Denominations are correctly maintained — output fees stored with tokenOut denomination, transferred as tokenOut. No cross-denomination confusion.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Dust-loop extraction via 100+ tiny swaps compounding rounding errors
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SwapMath.sol uses standard Uniswap V3 rounding: amountIn rounds UP, amountOut rounds DOWN. Dust accumulates in pool's favor, not attacker's. Each iteration loses the attacker dust, not gains.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: N/A — code review of SwapMath.sol rounding

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Forged hook caller — call hook directly bypassing AMM with fake pool identity
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All hook entry points (beforeSwap, afterSwap, beforeAddLiquidity, afterAddLiquidity) call _requireCallerIsAMM() which checks msg.sender == address(AMM). Hook cannot be called by anyone other than the AMM contract.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: N/A — code review of AMMStandardHook.sol lines 110, 159, 253, 312

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Permit mutation — replay permit signature with mutated feeOnTop (unsigned field) to redirect funds
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeOnTop is NOT in SWAP_TYPEHASH by design. The executor (msg.sender) supplies feeOnTop via calldata. Protection is via: (1) cosigner validation of executor, (2) hook validation, (3) limitAmount slippage protection. Without cosigner (address(0)), signer explicitly opts out of executor control. This is documented as a known design property.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: N/A — code review of PermitTransferHandler.sol and Constants.sol line 35

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Storage-slot collision — deploy facet that writes to another facet's storage slot
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Only admin can add facets to the diamond proxy. All legitimate facets use structured storage at slot 0x9A1D via Storage.appStorage(). No external attacker can deploy custom facets.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Transient-slot theft — re-enter collectHookFeesByHook during _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers to double-claim fees
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CEI pattern: _transferHookFeesByHook decrements tokensOwed BEFORE calling safeTransfer (line 3129). Re-entering collectHookFeesByHook during callback routes to direct transfer (flags cleared), but tokensOwed already reflects the deduction. Underflow check at line 3130 catches over-withdrawal.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: CLOB settlement callback reads AMM state before swap finalizes
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOBTransferHandler.ammHandleTransfer is called during _finalizeSwapCollectFundsAndDisburse, which is AFTER pool state (reserves, tick, price) is already updated. The CLOB handler also has its own nonReentrant guard and msg.sender == AMM check.

Exploit HOOK-001 stale transient slot to bypass pricing bounds on direct swap, then extract value from mispriced swap
